brief: US 10-year Treasury yields rose 100bp in 2026 while global equities gained about 13%, a combination Morgan Stanley's Andrew Sheets frames through the Gordon Growth model (value = D/(r-g)): rising r should compress valuations unless growth expectations g rise even faster to hold the gap steady. Sheets argues that is what happened. US median S&P 500 EPS growth is running mid-teens, Europe's 2026 EPS growth is around 20% with the median stock over 10%, and Asia/EM saw a net 21-point skew to earnings beats and an 11-point skew to EPS upgrades. The equity risk premium (S&P earnings yield minus Treasury yield) is broadly unchanged rather than lower. Two other channels show no activity yet: ETF flows stay positive and positively correlated across stocks and bonds, not rotating out of equities, and large tech issuers prefer debt over equity funding, with US IG issuance up 30% year-on-year through August and hyperscaler bond issuance over $220 billion this year. The earnings-yield/bond-yield gap has historically explained only about 10% of 12-month stock-bond performance, about half over three years, and Morgan Stanley has revised its yield forecasts higher on a more hawkish Fed view, raising the bar for earnings to keep growing this fast.
